subject: POC evaluation plan + GPU allocation (Aurora)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Kai Zhang <kai@aurora.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC planning follow-up: success criteria, GPUs & autoscale

Hi Kai —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed plan so we’re aligned before the engineering kick-off next week. I’ve pulled out owners & timelines so we can convert this to a mutual action plan if this looks good.

1) Success criteria (what Aurora will use to decide to move to Dedicated):
- Latency: 95th percentile generation time <= 180ms for 1k token batches during typical workload.
- Throughput: sustain 50 reqs/min with <5% error rate for 2-hour load test.
- Cost baseline: per-token inference cost within target range you shared ($0.0009 — please confirm).
- Quality: pass the 20 canonical prompt set (no>1 regression vs your baseline).

2) Evaluation plan & timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): exchange dataset extract + canonical prompts (Aurora) — deadline: Wed 5/12 EOD.
- Week 1: Redwood spins up trial environment; smoke test and run initial 2-hour load profile (Dev).
- Week 2: Joint run of acceptance test and qualitative eval (Aurora + Redwood).
- Decision review: Fri 5/28 — thumbs up / iterate / stop.

3) Capacity ask (initial proposal from Redwood):
- Reserved baseline: 2x A100-equivalent GPUs (for determinism during eval windows).
- Autoscaling: allow burst to 6 GPUs for up to 30 minutes for stress/runaway-burst tests (policy: scale up 30s, scale down 2m idle).
- KV-cache and prefix caching recommended for your chat flows — will reduce steady-state GPU requirement by ~25% (details in attached estimate).

4) Ownership & next steps:
- Aurora deliverable: dataset extract + canonical prompt set + cost target confirmation (Kai / procurement).
- Redwood deliverable: capacity estimate doc + trial environment link + test script (Dev).
- Kick-off: proposed Mon 5/17 10:00 PT for environment handoff.

Attachments: aurora_poc_requirements.xlsx (you), redwood_poc_capacity_estimate.pdf (us) — see the capacity doc for the assumed model family & quantization profile.

If that schedule works, I’ll convert to a shared M.A.P. and send calendar invites.

Thanks,
Soojin

Subject: Re: POC planning follow-up: success criteria, GPUs & autoscale

Thanks Soojin — this is great and captures the discussion. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The cost target I quoted earlier was for our current hosted provider; our internal goal for POC is $0.001/token (we can be flexible if performance gains justify a higher number).
- For the canonical prompt set: we’ll share 25 prompts (mix of short/long) by EOD Wed; we’ll also include 2 long tail prompts that tend to spike latency.
- Regarding GPUs: 2 baseline + burst to 6 sounds reasonable. Can we request that burst be rate-limited per-account so a single noisy test doesn’t consume the entire pool? If so, please outline limits.

Also looping in procurement (procurement@aurora.ai) for the commercial side — they’ll need the estimate and a draft MSA attachment to move paperwork.

— Kai
Kai Zhang
Lead ML Platform Engineer | Aurora AI Labs
kai@aurora.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC planning follow-up: success criteria, GPUs & autoscale

Hi Kai —

Quick follow-up on the capacity controls and a couple of technical asks so we size things correctly: 

1) Burst & rate-limits
- We can implement per-account burst caps: default = 6 GPUs max, per-account concurrent GPU cap = 3, and a per-second token emission cap (configurable) to avoid noisy floods.
- We’ll add a guard that prevents two independent bursts from the same account overlapping beyond the concurrent cap.

2) Reserved capacity windows
- For determinism during acceptance tests we’ll pin 2 GPUs for the time window you select. Recommended test window is 60–90 minutes. Please confirm preferred test window when you send the prompts.

3) Environment & access
- We’ll create a trial project in the Redwood Console and provision API keys scoped to the POC (keys expire after 30 days).
- Please confirm CIDR ranges for your testers so we can restrict access.

4) Test plan artifacts attached
- Attached: redwood_poc_capacity_estimate.pdf — includes assumed model family (Redwood-7B-Chat quantized), expected token throughput, and cost estimate.

If that works I’ll provision a baseline pool and share the console link by EOD Mon.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Staff Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai
